subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Maths simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Find the mean of 5, 9, 11, 7.
Find the mode of 3, 5, 5, 7, 9, 5, 2.
questions.explain: The mode is the most frequent value; 5 appears three times.

questions.q: The median of 3, x, 8, 11 (in order) is 6.5. Find x.
questions.explain: The median of four ordered values is (x + 8)/2 = 6.5, so x + 8 = 13 and x = 5.

questions.q: Goals per match: 0 (freq 5), 1 (freq 8), 2 (freq 7). Find the mean number of goals.
Values 10 (freq 2), 20 (freq 3), 30 (freq 5). Find the mean.
Groups: 0-20 (freq 4, mid 10), 20-40 (freq 6, mid 30). Estimate the mean.
Why is the mean from grouped data only an estimate?
options: Exact values in each class are unknown, so midpoints are used
questions.explain: We do not know each individual value, only its class, so we assume every value equals the midpoint, giving an estimate.

questions.q: Stratified sampling divides the population into groups before sampling. What is done next?
options: Sample each group in proportion to its size
Sample the same number from each group
questions.explain: In stratified sampling the number taken from each stratum is proportional to that stratum's share of the population.

questions.q: A school has 300 girls and 200 boys. A stratified sample of 50 is taken. How many girls?
questions.explain: Girls are 300/500 of the school. 300/500 × 50 = 30 girls.

questions.q: A pictogram uses one symbol = 4 cars. How many symbols show 14 cars?
questions.explain: 14 ÷ 4 = 3.5, so three and a half symbols.

questions.q: In a pie chart of 90 people, one sector is 60°. How many people does it represent?
A histogram bar has frequency density 6 over a class of width 5. Find the frequency.
questions.explain: Frequency = frequency density × class width = 6 × 5 = 30.

questions.q: Why are histograms used instead of bar charts for grouped continuous data with unequal widths?
options: Bars must be the same colour
Area represents frequency, so widths are handled fairly
questions.explain: In a histogram the area of each bar is proportional to frequency, correctly handling unequal class widths.

questions.q: A box plot shows minimum 5, Q1 15, median 22, Q3 30, maximum 45. Find the IQR.
On a cumulative frequency graph for 80 values, the upper quartile is read at which cumulative frequency?
questions.explain: The upper quartile Q3 is at 3n/4 = 3×80/4 = 60.

questions.q: Height and shoe size tend to increase together. What correlation is this?
questions.explain: When both variables increase together, the correlation is positive.

questions.q: Correlation between two variables does NOT necessarily mean what?
options: That a line of best fit can be drawn
questions.explain: Correlation does not imply causation; a relationship in data does not prove one variable causes the other.

questions.q: Using a line of best fit to predict a y-value for an x-value within the data range is called what?
questions.explain: Estimating within the range of the data is interpolation, which is generally reliable.

questions.q: Class A has median 60 and IQR 8; Class B has median 55 and IQR 20. Which is more consistent?
options: Class A, because its IQR is smaller
Class A, because its median is higher
Class B, because its median is lower
questions.explain: A smaller IQR means less spread, so Class A is more consistent.

questions.q: Which measure of spread is least affected by outliers?
questions.explain: The IQR uses only the middle 50% of data, so extreme outliers do not affect it, unlike the range.
